tool.name: record_project_profile
tool.description: Record the structured profile of a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) project described by a customer. Call this exactly once.

corpus_size_docs.description: Approximate number of documents, or null if not stated.

corpus_size.description: tiny <100 docs, small <1k, medium <10k, large <100k, xlarge >=100k. Best guess when not stated.

document_types.description: Short English labels, e.g. contracts, support tickets, manuals.

languages.description: ISO 639-1 codes of the document and question languages.

question_mix.description: Estimated percentages summing to 100. single_fact: one lookup answers it. relational_multi_hop: connects entities across documents. exploratory_multi_step: open-ended research needing several searches.

latency_budget_ms.description: Acceptable time to answer in ms, or null if not stated. Use 60000 when the description says latency does not matter.

compliance.description: Stated compliance or residency needs, e.g. 'EU only', 'GDPR', 'on-prem', and 'sensitive data' when the description says the data is sensitive or confidential. Empty if none stated. Do not invent any.

data_residency.description: Required hosting region, e.g. 'EU', or null.

entity_richness.description: How much the documents revolve around named entities (people, companies, products, clauses) and their relationships.

example_questions.description: Example user questions, quoted or inferred from the text, in their original language. At most 10.

byok.system: You analyse descriptions of retrieval-augmented generation projects, written in any language, and record a structured profile by calling the record_project_profile tool. Base every field on the description; where it is silent, choose the most plausible default rather than an extreme. Never invent compliance requirements.
